title: The Big Bang of 1687

panels.visual: The Parthenon gleaming new with painted sculptures, 432 BC, Athenians carrying offerings up to it
panels.caption: The Parthenon was built as a temple to Athena, finished in 432 BC.

panels.visual: The Parthenon around AD 600 with a bell, Christian priests and a cross on top, candles inside
panels.caption: About a thousand years later it became a Christian church.

panels.visual: The Parthenon around 1460 with a slender minaret tower rising from one corner, Ottoman Turks in turbans praying inside
panels.caption: When the Ottoman Turks took Athens, it became a mosque. For two thousand years it still had its roof.

panels.visual: 1687: Venetian soldiers in tricorn hats and armour dragging cannons up the hill opposite the Acropolis, their general Morosini (grey moustache) pointing
panels.caption: In 1687 a Venetian army under General Morosini attacked the Turks on the Acropolis.

panels.visual: Ottoman soldiers rolling barrels marked with a gunpowder symbol into the dark Parthenon, women and children sheltering inside too
panels.caption: The Turks stored their gunpowder in the Parthenon. They thought it was the strongest building there. Families sheltered inside too.

panels.visual: Night, 26 September 1687: a Venetian mortar firing, a glowing shell arcing across the dark sky towards the Acropolis
panels.caption: On the night of 26 September 1687, a Venetian shell flew over the walls...

panels.visual: The shell crashing through the Parthenon's roof among the gunpowder barrels, sparks flying
panels.caption: ...and fell through the roof, right onto the gunpowder.

panels.visual: A gigantic explosion blowing the middle of the Parthenon apart, columns and roof flying, orange fire against the night
panels.caption: The middle of the Parthenon blew apart.

panels.visual: Smoke over the broken Parthenon at dawn, the long sides with a huge gap in the middle, rubble everywhere
panels.caption: About three hundred people died. The roof, many columns and carvings were gone.

panels.visual: Morosini's soldiers trying to lower carved horse statues from the pediment with ropes; the ropes snap and the statues smash on the ground
panels.caption: Morosini tried to take statues home as trophies. His men dropped them and they smashed.

panels.visual: Around 1801: Lord Elgin's workmen sawing carved marble panels off the ruin and crating them up for a ship
panels.caption: More than a hundred years later, Lord Elgin's men took many of the carvings to London.

panels.visual: Today: the Parthenon covered in scaffolding with cranes and restorers, the gap in the side clearly visible, Glauka on a column
panels.caption: Look at the long sides: you can see the gap. It's a ruin because of an explosion, not old age.

speech.speaker: Glauka
speech.text: Gunpowder in a temple. Bad idea.

mood: Dramatic war mood: smoke, fire, night sky lit orange, one orange-red accent colour; no gore; suitable for children aged 9 to 11.
